prompt:
Create a production-quality painted fantasy RPG character animation sheet by painting over image 1's EXACT 24 source poses, one coherent COMPLETE clothed character in EVERY cell. Image 1 is the binding actual Blender Mesh2Motion motion/camera guide. Image 2 is our approved design study for the male Mage facing SW; use its red/auburn hair, face, tall body proportions, navy-and-ivory gold-trimmed coat, belts, gloves, boots, and wooden turquoise-crystal staff. Use the earlier tall illustrated Swordsman-quality detailed hand-painted fantasy finish: clean contours, rich restrained shading, clear material highlights, readable anatomy, not compact chibi, no blurry airbrush.
The layout MUST be FOUR columns and SIX rows, 24 cells in exact row-major pose order, portrait 2:3 canvas. Every cell is an actual distinct consecutive source pose; do not invent, reorder, mirror, omit, repeat, rotate the camera or fit each figure independently. Lock the camera, body scale, limb lengths, proportions and common cell/root placement to the guide. The full source sequence is Spell_Simple_Enter > Spell_Simple_Shoot > Spell_Simple_Exit. The staff stays in the guide's anatomical RIGHT hand and the anatomical LEFT hand casts. The guide's actual arm/hand/foot/staff placement overrides the static identity picture's convenience pose. In particular do not swap which hand holds the staff or blindly copy the identity's arm pose. Trace visible foreshortening and elbow/knee bends carefully. Keep fingers wrapped around the same shaft pivot in EVERY frame. The small T/cross at the proxy grip is a rig reference, not a sword hilt: paint a natural staff-holding glove there, with no crossguard. Replace the proxy's wooden shaft with our identity's elegant wooden turquoise-crystal staff, preserving its grip and projected shaft direction.
Draw the ENTIRE connected clothed body, with all arms, hands, legs and boots together, plus the same head/hair and held staff. This will be cut into BodyCostume, HeadHair and Weapon only AFTER the complete frame is coherent. No separate limb tiles, pasted limbs, missing necks, extra hands/feet, detached equipment, independently sliding boots or costume changes between frames. Maintain stable face, head size and coat lengths throughout. Clear true air gaps between arms and staff, not opaque white triangular wedges. All characters and staff tips fit safely inside their own cell, with equal framing. White/transparent plain background, no scene, ground, shadow, trail, magic VFX, grid lines, labels or frame numbers in the OUTPUT. High clarity, crisp native painted detail, no decorative poster layout. Follow the real rear/side occlusion in SW; do not turn a rear view into a front portrait. The guide alone controls geometry; image 2 controls design and materials.
